results.title: Seattle Tree Inspection Priority — Portfolio Simmulation v2
results.description:
Portfolio demonstration dataset.

This hosted feature layer simulates a municipal urban forestry
inspection prioritization workflow.

Analysis includes

• Tree inventory QA/QC
• DBH estimation hierarchy
• Derived maturity classes
• Simulated inspection history
• Proximity to sidewalks
• Proximity to arterial streets
• Proximity to schools
• Proximity to trails
• Seattle Racial & Social Equity Index
• Weighted inspection priority model
• Five-year inspection scheduling

All condition ratings, inspection history, and maintenance
priorities are simulated for educational and portfolio purposes.
results.snippet: Simulated municipal tree inspection prioritization dataset for Seattle Parks. Combines inventory condition, DBH-derived maturity, equity context, and proximity to public infrastructure into a reproducible GIS asset-management workflow.
results.accessInformation: City of Seattle Open Data; portfolio analysis and simulation fields by project author.
results.licenseInfo: Sourse datasets retain their original terms. Analysis ouputs are for demonstration only.

results.title: Seeing Seattle, WA
results.description: Discovery Park is the largest city park in Seattle, WA. Seattle Parks and Recreation oversees this 534 acre site, offering fantastic views as well as opportunities for recreation and community engagement. The park sits on top of Magnolia Bluff and overlooks Puget Sound, as well as the Olympic and Cascade mountain ranges. It has a unique combination of terrain such as tidal beaches, open meadow lands, dramatic sea cliffs, forest groves, active sand dunes, thickets and streams. Due to its natural diversity, the park hosts a variety of wildlife from coyotes to sea lions. The space also provides a chance for city-dwellers to escape the hustle and bustle of Seattle and slow down in a natural and serene environment. Discovery Park was most recently upgraded in 2017 with better and safer play equipment, as well as increased accessibility according to the Americans with Disabilities Act.
results.snippet: An exploration of Seattle's most iconic features and history.

About the data: The Congressional districts: Health and socioeconomic profiles layer contains information about each congressional district’s representative in Congress and detailed health, socioeconomic, and demographic data for the district. This layer is included in Earthjustice Action's Community Health Atlas: An Environmental Impacts Mapping Tool. 

Purpose: The purpose of the Community Health Atlas is to  make it easier for partners in the environmental community to develop effective messaging for members of Congress (MOCs) that focuses on the specific concerns and sensitive populations in each congressional district. The Atlas is not a screening tool. It does not rank communities or calculate environmental justice scores. It is a tool to facilitate gathering congressional district information that our partners can use to tailor their advocacy message to address the issues of concern in each MOCs district.

Data sources:

Data field
• High blood pressure among adults
• Cancer (non-skin) or melanoma among adults
• Current asthma among adults
• Coronary heart disease among adults
• Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) among adults
• Diagnosed diabetes among adults
• Stroke among adults
• Fair or poor self-rated health status among adults
• Frequent mental distress among adults
• Frequent physical distress among adults
• Lack of health insurance among adults aged 18-64 years
• Routine checkup within the past year among adults
• Any disability among adults
• Received food stamps in the past 12 months among adults
• Food insecurity in the past 12 months among adults
• Housing insecurity in the past 12 months among adults
• Lack of reliable transportation in the past 12 months among adults

(Note: The CDC derived the above model-based estimates using Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) 2022 or 2021 data, Census Bureau 2022 county population estimate data, and American Community Survey 2018–2022 estimates.)

Source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, Census Tract Data 2024 release. https://data.cdc.gov/browse?category=500+Cities+%26+Places&q=2024&sortBy=relevance&tags=places&pageSize=20. Accessed May 27, 2026.

Source: CDC. 2023 Child Current Asthma Prevalence and Number by State. https://www.cdc.gov/asthma-data/nsch-prevalence/index.html#cdc_data_surveillance_section_2-2023. Accessed September 1, 2026.

Source: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME). United States Health Care Spending by Health Condition and County 2010-2019. Seattle, United States of America: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME), 2025. Obtained by request. Thanks to Dr. Joseph Dieleman and Mr. Drew DeJarnatt. [Detailed data for 2018 a were obtained from the researchers and used to develop our estimates of spending on asthma and cancer treatment per congressional district.]

Data sources used to calculate estimates of costs for asthma and cancer treatment by congressional district:

Data type

Source: Song HJ, Blake KV, Wilson DL, Winterstein AG, Park H. Medical Costs and Productivity Loss Due to Mild, Moderate, and Severe Asthma in the United States. J Asthma Allergy. 2020 Oct 29;13:545-555. doi: 10.2147/JAA.S272681. PMID: 33149626; PMCID: PMC7605920

results.title: geog258-project2
results.description: In the age of COVID-19 and heavy restrictions on activities. Parks have been an important destination for members of society who are tired of being stuck at home. According to Google COVID-19 Community Mobility Reports, parks saw as high as 86% higher mobility changes compared to baseline throughout the 2020 spring, summer, and early fall in the United States. Parks offer a greenspace that can be used for many purposes such as exercise in an environment that allows for social distancing. With these places increasing in popularity due to the coronavirus, accessibility becomes an important issue. How accessible are parks to people with disabilities? More specifically, how accessible are parks to wheelchair users in Seattle?
